En 1955, près du village de Pesse, aux P: In 1955, near the village of Pesse, in the Netherlands, a team building a road pulls a hollowed trunk out of a peat bog. It is a canoe, carved from a single pine trunk, about 3 meters long.
It dates from between 8250 and 7550 BC: it is the oldest known boat. It can be seen at the Drents Museum.
Le plus vieux bateau connu : la pirogue: The oldest known boat: the Pesse canoe (Netherlands), a pine trunk hollowed out about 10,000 years ago.
Le plus vieux bateau retrouvé n'est pas: The oldest boat found is not the first boat. There is solid evidence that humans lived in Australia 50,000 to 65,000 years ago, the archaeologist Mikael Fauvelle points out. To get there, they had to cross the sea: so there were boats about 50,000 years ago.
Certains vont beaucoup plus loin. Sur l': Some go much further. On the island of Flores, tools dated to about 800,000 years ago led Michael Morwood's team to say, in 1998, that Homo erectus may already have had a boat. On Crete, tools are said to be at least 130,000 years old, but these dates are disputed.
Des humains sont en Australie il y a au: Humans are in Australia at least 50,000 years ago: they crossed the sea. Boats are much older than the Pesse one.
Les navigateurs du Pacifique traversaien: Pacific navigators crossed the ocean without instruments. At night, they took as landmarks the points on the horizon where stars and planets rise and set. By day, the sun. In overcast weather, the swell and the direction of the wind. Routes were learned by heart, or kept in songs.
Ils lisaient aussi la couleur et la form: They also read the color and shape of clouds, and the birds: boobies, terns or petrels out fishing say that land is near. Their boats had changed. An outrigger fixed to the side makes the canoe faster and more stable; double-hulled canoes, about 20 to 36 meters long, can handle rougher seas.
Dans le Pacifique, on navigue aux étoile: In the Pacific, people navigate by stars that rise and set, by the swell, the clouds and fishing birds.
